variants.linkedin:
Social entrepreneurship is getting better at measuring impact. The harder question is what happens next: who will actually pay for the outcomes we can prove?

Three current signals point in the same direction: the World Economic Forum and Schwab Foundation are calling for a shift from impact disclosure to economic demand; Social Finance has just announced two impact-first investments in overlooked markets; and social-innovation practitioners, funders and policymakers are meeting in Nairobi for Wayfinder.

For African founders, the practical lesson is to connect impact to the enterprise model. Who experiences the value? Who pays? What evidence changes a buyer or investor decision? What kind of capital fits the next stage?

I explore the implications here:
https://www.waithakandegwa.com/my-thoughts/from-impact-evidence-to-economic-demand

#SocialEntrepreneurship #ImpactInvesting #Africa #Kenya #SocialInnovation
variants.facebook:
Measuring impact is important. But a social enterprise still has to answer a more difficult question: who values that impact enough to buy, fund, procure or invest in the solution?

This week offers useful signals—from impact-first investment decisions to the Wayfinder social-innovation gathering in Nairobi. The emerging conversation is moving beyond disclosure towards demand.

For African entrepreneurs, that means being clearer about customers, beneficiaries, evidence, unit economics and the type of capital that actually fits the enterprise.

New analysis:
https://www.waithakandegwa.com/my-thoughts/from-impact-evidence-to-economic-demand
variants.instagram:
Impact measurement is not the finish line.

A social enterprise can prove that it creates value and still struggle to finance growth. The next question is whether that value influences a real economic decision: a purchase, procurement contract, investment, grant, policy incentive or partnership.

Current signals—from the impact-economy debate to Wayfinder Nairobi—suggest that social entrepreneurship is entering a more demanding phase.

For African founders: know who benefits, who pays, what evidence matters, and what capital fits the next stage.

Read the full article at waithakandegwa.com.

#SocialEntrepreneurship #SocialInnovation #ImpactInvesting #Africa #Kenya
